- Ebola virus disease (EVD) outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) has surpassed 1,000 deaths, with 1,033 fatalities among 2,535 confirmed cases as of 23 July 2026. Of the confirmed cases, 738 are in isolation and 506 have recovered; the overall case-fatality rate is 40.7%. The national contact-tracing rate stands at 77.2%, below targets. The outbreak affects 42 health zones across five provinces: Nord-Kivu, Sud-Kivu, Ituri, Tshopo, and Haut-Uele. Ituri remains the hotspot, accounting for 88.6% of cumulative cases and 73% of new infections recorded on the day. Nord-Kivu has the highest case-fatality rate at 58.7%. The Emergency Operations Centre for Patient Care notes ongoing transmission, with the outbreak having begun on May 15.
- An Ebola outbreak in Africa has claimed more than 1,000 lives. In the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), as of July 20, there are 2,473 laboratory-confirmed cases, including 999 deaths and 482 recoveries. Uganda reports 20 confirmed cases, including 2 deaths, bringing total deaths across the two countries to 1,001. The outbreak is caused by Bundibugyo ebolavirus and remains in a sustained transmission phase with high viral circulation. Frontline responders have been infected in 121 cases, with 36 deaths. WHO cautions that official figures may underestimate the true scale; modeling suggests the real burden could be 2–4 times higher. articleSummary: Floods in Accra and flood-affected communities heighten diarrhoeal risk among children.
